_comment: Voice-over and layout for the hackathon demo video. Built by demo/build.mjs.

segments.title: Outward
segments.subtitle: Your story happens outside.
segments.vo: This is Outward: a story you can only play by going outside. You put your phone in your pocket and walk. When you find something real, a small AI running entirely on your phone weaves it into the story. No signal needed, no cloud, and almost no screen time.

segments.title: Meet Sprig
segments.subtitle: Your walking companion
segments.vo: Meet Sprig, your walking companion. Tap Start Adventure, and the Archivist reads the chapter. That voice was made with ElevenLabs and saved on the phone, so it plays with no signal.

segments.title: A real-world mission
segments.subtitle: Safe by design, then pocket the phone
segments.vo: Every chapter has a safe mission. Pick your time, pocket the phone, and walk. GPS counts the distance, and the I found it button only opens once you have really walked.

segments.title: AI on the phone
segments.subtitle: Airplane mode on
segments.vo: This part runs in airplane mode. You say or type what you found. Then Sprig thinks, and my distilled Gemma model writes the next part of the story right on the phone, in about two seconds, using your own words.

segments.title: Proud of the walk
segments.subtitle: Minutes outside, not on screen
segments.vo: Back home, the trophy is the number that matters: minutes outside against minutes on screen. You earn XP, badges, and a journal card for everything you found.

segments.title: A story that grows
segments.subtitle: Quest map and story packs
segments.vo: Chapters form a trail on the quest map, and new story packs come from a story factory on Render, reviewed by a person before they ship.

segments.title: Open models, made smaller
segments.subtitle: Tinker teacher, distilled Gemma student
segments.vo: Every model here is open. I fine-tuned Qwen 3.5, four billion parameters, on Tinker, then distilled it into Gemma 3 with 270 million. On fifty held-out prompts, stock Gemma scored 2.6 out of 5. My distilled model scored 4.75, almost matching its teacher, with fewer unsafe outputs. All the Tinker training cost two dollars fifty-six.
